Description
Our client, a mid-sized German chemicals group (approx. 3,200 employees), has signed the acquisition of a Dutch-Belgian specialty coatings company with around 700 employees and two plants. Closing is expected in early November 2026. The client has limited integration experience and is looking for an interim PMI Lead who sets up the Integration Management Office and drives the integration for the first nine months after closing.

The integration covers commercial integration (sales channels, key accounts, pricing), operations and supply chain, finance and reporting, HR and the IT landscape (the target runs Microsoft Dynamics, the buyer SAP S/4HANA). The synergy case in the deal model is EUR 18 million per year by 2028, mostly procurement and SG&A synergies.

Tasks
• Set up and run the Integration Management Office (IMO) and the integration governance with a steering committee chaired by the CFO
• Build the integration master plan with the workstream leads and track milestones, dependencies and risks
• Day 1 and first 100 days plan, including communication with employees, customers and suppliers
• Synergy tracking and reporting (baseline, initiatives, realisation) together with group controlling
• Coordinate the IT integration roadmap and the harmonisation of core processes
• Support cultural integration and change management across both companies
• Weekly status to the executive board, monthly steering committee preparation

Requirements
• Several years of experience as PMI lead, IMO lead or integration programme manager, ideally after acquisitions in the chemical or process industry
• Proven track record in synergy tracking and programme governance
• Experience with transitional services (TSA) between seller and buyer is a plus, since some services will be provided by the seller for up to 12 months
• Strong stakeholder management at board level, structured and pragmatic
• Fluent English and German, Dutch is a plus

Conditions
Interim assignment, full-time, about half of the time on site in Leverkusen and at the plants in Belgium and the Netherlands. Start 16 November 2026, runs until 31 August 2027. Rate EUR 175 per hour plus travel expenses. Freelance contract via Rheinschiene Consulting Network GmbH.
